title: Parallax — the road you did not take
style: cinematic still, 40mm anamorphic on ARRI Alexa 35, overcast dusk at high altitude, páramo light, wet asphalt holding specular highlights, volumetric mist between ridgelines, desaturated slate and moss palette, fine film grain, deep atmospheric perspective, photographic not illustrative
negative: text, lettering, signage copy, watermark, people, vehicles, animals, illustration, oversaturated, HDR halos, low quality, warped geometry

scenes.title: Every operational change is a bet.
scenes.body: You ship it, and then you find out.
scenes.image: wide low shot down an empty two-lane highland road at dusk, centre line receding into mist, moss-dark ridgelines layered on both sides, wet asphalt catching the last light, no vehicles and no signage

scenes.title: This is where it happened.
scenes.body: A price, a policy, a promise. One decision, at one moment, on one line of the log.
scenes.image: medium shot of a weathered concrete kilometre marker standing at the roadside, blank and unlettered, wet grass at its base, the road continuing past it into shallow fog, shallow depth of field on the marker

scenes.title: You found out from a customer.
scenes.body: By the time the damage is legible it has already landed.
scenes.image: the road ahead blocked by a fresh landslide of dark earth and rock spilling across both lanes, a single amber hazard lamp glowing at the edge, mist heavy above the debris, ridgeline barely visible behind

scenes.title: So go back to it.
scenes.body: Your operations already run on an append-only history. A history can be forked.
scenes.image: reverse view along the same road looking back toward the kilometre marker, the blockage now out of frame behind, mist closing over the receding asphalt, cool even dusk light

scenes.title: Run it again. Change one thing.
scenes.body: Same customers, same inventory, same hour. One policy different.
scenes.image: the single carriageway widening and dividing into two identical lanes separated by a low grass median, camera centred on the split, both roads receding symmetrically into mist

scenes.title: Now you can see both.
scenes.body: And every number says how much of it was real.
scenes.image: elevated wide shot of two roads pulled far apart across a broad valley, cloud breaking to pale light over the left carriageway while rain still falls on the right, ridgelines receding in atmospheric layers

motions: Camera glides forward low over the centre line at walking pace, mist parting ahead of it; the marker enters from the right and settles into frame as the road continues past.
Forward dolly accelerates gently down the road, the far bend resolving into blocked carriageway; the camera slows to a stop as the hazard lamp pulses once.
Camera reverses smoothly back along the road, the blockage receding out of focus behind, mist closing over it until the marker returns to frame.
Slow forward push past the marker; the single carriageway widens and separates, a low median emerging between two identical lanes while the camera holds dead centre.
Camera rises slightly and holds steady as the two roads pull apart across the valley, cloud breaking over the left carriageway while rain stays on the right.
